root_cause: Carbon monoxide poisoning from a faulty gas heater

patient.name: Lena Okafor
patient.background: Engineering student, healthy, new basement flat with old gas heater, migraine history

findings.result: Carboxyhemoglobin 28%; CO stuck where oxygen should ride
Finger oxygen reads normal 99%, misleading (pulse oximetry)
Mild heart muscle strain, slightly raised troponin
Brain cells starved of oxygen, early hypoxia changes
High lactate: tissues burning fuel without oxygen
Clear lungs, no pneumonia or clot (normal X-ray)
Irritated lining from caffeine, mild gastritis
Normal color, no rash or cyanosis

treatments.name: 100% high-flow oxygen
treatments.why: Pure oxygen pushes CO off hemoglobin, cutting its half-life from ~5 hours to ~1 hour.
treatments.attending_line: Oxygen. For someone who can't get oxygen. Groundbreaking, but correct.

treatments.name: Sumatriptan for migraine
treatments.why: Triptans narrow blood vessels, starving an already oxygen-starved heart.
treatments.attending_line: Yes, squeeze the arteries of the oxygen-starved heart. Bold.

treatments.name: Antibiotics for viral flu
treatments.why: No infection exists; CO keeps building while she goes home to the heater.
treatments.attending_line: Flu doesn't give the roommate the same headache at the same address.

treatments.name: Lorazepam for anxiety
treatments.why: Sedation slows breathing, so less oxygen comes in and CO clears even slower.
treatments.attending_line: She's not panicking, she's suffocating. Calming her won't fix that.

post_mortem: Lena's old basement gas heater was leaking carbon monoxide, which binds hemoglobin 200 times more tightly than oxygen and slowly suffocated her tissues. The giveaways were a roommate with the same symptoms, feeling better away from home, and a "normal" finger oxygen reading that can't tell CO from oxygen.
